topics.name: target_pose
topics.description: Desired end-effector pose, in the root component's frame. In Studio this is bound to the scene's IK gizmo so dragging the handle drives the solver.

topics.name: joint_states
topics.description: Current joint states for every joint in the chain. Used as the seed for the next solve.

topics.name: joint_commands
topics.description: Per-joint target positions produced by the solver. Wire each into the corresponding Joint Controller.

topics.name: current_pose
topics.description: End-effector pose computed from joint_states via forward kinematics. Rendered as an overlay in the scene.

root_part_id.label: Root Part
root_part_id.description: Parts-built robot: a part on the chain's base body (usually the base part). The solver walks from its body to the end-effector part's body, and targets are expressed in this part's frame.

end_effector_part_id.label: End Effector Part
end_effector_part_id.description: Parts-built robot: the part whose frame is the tool point (a gripper palm, a foot). Any part welded to the tip body works; its own frame is what reaches the target.

root_component_id.label: Root Component (legacy)
root_component_id.description: The root (base) component of the kinematic chain. The solver walks downward from here toward the end-effector. Component-built robots only; a parts-built robot uses Root Part.

end_effector_component_id.label: End Effector (legacy)
end_effector_component_id.description: The tip component of the kinematic chain (e.g. hand, gripper). The solver builds a path from root to this component. Component-built robots only; a parts-built robot uses End Effector Part.

flat_articulation.label: Robot Bodies
flat_articulation.description: Auto-injected for a parts-built robot: its rigid bodies and the DOF joints between them (the physics worker's own articulation).

max_iterations.label: Max Solver Iterations
max_iterations.description: Maximum number of iterations for the IK solver.

damping.label: Damping Factor
damping.description: Damping factor (λ) for the damped least-squares solver. Higher values improve stability near singularities.
